preview.tournamentOverview: Sedgefield Country Club rewards ball-striking and approach play on its short, tight layout. SG App 8%) and SG Total 9%) dominate the model, while SG ATG 2%) and SG OTT The Wyndham is the final regular-season event, setting the field for the FedEx Cup Playoffs.
preview.modelExplainer: Approach play carries the heaviest weight at 8%, followed by SG Total at 9% and SG ATG at 2%. Driving accuracy 7%) and bogey avoidance 0%) receive minimal emphasis, reflecting Sedgefield's premium on iron play over raw distance or scrambling.
preview.pickApproach: We tier bets by model rank and power rank gaps, targeting players whose SG App and SG Total align with course demands. First tier includes top-10 model names with positive SG App; second tier adds SG ATG standouts outside the top 20.

article.title: Wyndham Championship Model Targets: Young, Matsuyama, Hisatsune Lead Sedgefield Field
article.dek: Tournament model ranks Cameron Young #1, Hideki Matsuyama #2, and Ryo Hisatsune #3 for the 147-player Wyndham field at Sedgefield Country Club.
article.introduction: The tournament model weights SG APP at 8% and SG Total at 9%, producing a top-20 list led by Cameron Young 574 SG Total, rank #1). Hideki Matsuyama 197 SG Total, rank #2) and Ryo Hisatsune 238 SG Total, rank #3) follow, each with model ranks well ahead of their power ranks.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: Sedgefield Country Club hosts the Wyndham Championship with course weights emphasizing SG APP 8%) and SG Total 9%). The model ranks 147 players using these weights, producing a top-20 list where the top three names sit well ahead of their power ranks.

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: Cameron Young's 499 SG APP and 699 SG OTT align with the 8% and 4% weights. Hideki Matsuyama's 635 SG APP and 39 SG ATG match the same emphasis. Ryo Hisatsune's 576 SG APP and 509 SG OTT also fit the weighted profile.

sections.heading: Recent Form
sections.body: The model uses the most recent rolling strokes-gained data to produce the listed ranks. Cameron Young's 574 SG Total leads the field, followed by Ryo Hisatsune at 238 and Hideki Matsuyama at 197.

sections.heading: Post-Open Workload
sections.body: Cameron Young, Hideki Matsuyama, and Ryo Hisatsune each show NO_TRACKED_ROUNDS from The Open Championship and Genesis Scottish Open. This classification indicates zero recorded rounds in those events; it does not confirm rest.

sections.heading: FedExCup Motivation
sections.body: Cameron Young enters at FedExCup rank #3, Hideki Matsuyama at #24, and Ryo Hisatsune at #42—all inside the top 50 and therefore SAFE_TOP_50. These positions place each player inside the automatic qualification zone for the next playoff event.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: Each of the three targets skipped the Scottish Open and holds a top-10 model rank. Cameron Young's model rank (#1) exceeds his power rank (#6) by five spots; Matsuyama's model rank (#2) exceeds his power rank (#16) by fourteen spots; Hisatsune's model rank (#3) exceeds his power rank (#20) by seventeen spots.

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: Cameron Young (model rank #1, 574 SG Total) and Hideki Matsuyama (model rank #2, 197 SG Total) are the two outright targets.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: Cameron Young, Hideki Matsuyama, and Ryo Hisatsune (model rank #3, 238 SG Total) form the top-10 card.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are unavailable. Workload coverage includes only recorded rounds from The Open Championship and Genesis Scottish Open; opposite-field, DP World Tour, LIV, and other events may be missing.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Tier 1 (model-supported): Cameron Young (rank #1). Tier 2 (model-supported): Hideki Matsuyama (rank #2), Ryo Hisatsune (rank #3).

article.conclusion: Model-supported outright and top-10 card: Cameron Young (Tier 1), Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune (Tier 2).

keyTakeaways.text: Cameron Young leads the model at rank #1 with 1.574 SG Total and sits #6 in power rank, creating the largest positive differential in the top 20.
Hideki Matsuyama posts 1.197 SG Total and ranks #2 in the model versus #16 power rank, driven by 0.635 SG APP and 0.39 SG ATG.
Ryo Hisatsune ranks #3 in the model with 1.238 SG Total and 0.576 SG APP, ahead of his #20 power rank.
All three targets carry zero tracked rounds from The Open and Scottish Open, with FedExCup ranks inside the top 50 (#3, #24, #42).
